recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any broader future guidance about Observation.device, implanted or influencing devices, preconditions, supportingInfo, or linked observations should be handled as a new scoped Jira rather than as further application of FHIR-43597.
issue_request: FHIR-43597 was an Applied/Persuasive OO change request for FHIR-core Observation asking to clarify whether vital-signs device qualifier notes such as 8887-2 Heart rate device type meant component observations or separate sibling/panel/hasMember observations.
initial_application: No searched source commit explicitly mentioned FHIR-43597. The relevant wording appears to have been applied through the related FHIR-32787 vitals-table clarification commit f5ab9c158d, which changed the affected rows from additional observation(s) to additional component observation(s).
additional_context: The Observation resource and the core vitals IG are active build inputs. FHIR-46418 previously reworked the vital-signs profile page, and FHIR-32787 later clarified the component-observation wording. The 2025-10-23 OO Main minutes list FHIR-43597 as Persuasive in the final block vote with an 8-0-2 approval motion; Zulip searches found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current source at source/observation/observation-vitalsigns-profile-introduction.xml already says the heart-rate, body-temperature, and blood-pressure qualifier codes may be used as additional component observations, matching the submitter's final Jira comment that the concern was closed.

related_jiras.note: Its applied vitals-table clarification introduced the component-observation wording that resolves the FHIR-43597 ambiguity.
